newsitem.title: USA: Workers facing layoffs win $46 million in lottery.
newsitem.headline: Workers facing layoffs win $46 million in lottery.

text.p: A group of Michigan factory workers who were preparing for impending layoffs reported to work as usual on Monday, even after a lottery ticket they bought won a $46 million jackpot on Friday.
Shirley Johnson said she and her 16 previously unlucky co-workers would continue "to work until we get our pink slip."

Kellogg Industries Co., a surgical and orthopedic supplies plant in Jackson, Michigan, that was scheduled to close in June, notified its 85 workers last November that it would close the 90-year-old facility and transfer production to a newer plant in California.
Two weeks ago, some of the workers formed a lottery club and bought 19 tickets for Friday's "Big Game" multi-state lottery.

"A lot of these people are single mothers that didn't know what they were going to do without a job," she said in a telephone interview. "We're not going to celebrate until we get that check in our hands."
Johnson said she lit two candles for the group every time she went to church.
The $46 million jackpot will provide each of the 17 winners with an annual check of about $135,000, before taxes, for 20 years, or a total of $2.7 million.
Johnson, 53, who is married with children and grandchildren, said most of the winners have modest spending plans, including improvements to existing homes, new car purchases and charitable donations.

The payout was the largest since the Big Game began on Nov. 29, 1996. The lottery, played in Massachusetts, Michigan, Illinois, Georgia, Maryland and Virginia, calls for a match of five numbers from 1 to 50, plus another between 1 and 25.
